summary: Checking often is praised for women. Women who cannot check for themselves can be helped by others. It also tells how careful Jewish women are to check.

chunks.he: כָּל הַיָּד הַמַּרְבָּה לִבְדֹּק בְּנָשִׁים, מְשֻׁבַּחַת.
chunks.en: Any hand that checks a lot is praised for women.
chunks.st: With regard to any hand that is diligent to examine bodily emissions to ascertain ritual impurity, among women such a hand is praiseworthy.

chunks.en: But for men, it should be cut off.
chunks.explain: For men it is not a good thing.
chunks.st: But among men such a hand should be severed,
chunks.stMore: as this action is apt to lead to a seminal emission for naught. In the case of a woman

chunks.en: A woman who cannot hear or speak, a woman who cannot think clearly, a blind woman, and a woman who lost her mind,
chunks.st: who is deaf [haḥereshet], or an imbecile, or blind, or who went insane,

words.en: and the woman who cannot think clearly

chunks.en: if they have women with clear minds,
chunks.st: and is therefore unable to examine herself reliably, if

chunks.en: those women get them ready, and they may eat terumah.
chunks.st: such women have competent friends, those friends prepare them by examining them and immersing them in a ritual bath. And on that basis the incompetent women may partake of teruma

chunks.en: The way of Jewish women
chunks.st: after the sun sets. It is the custom of Jewish women

chunks.en: is to use two checking cloths,
chunks.st: that they engage in intercourse with their husbands while using two examination cloths, one for

chunks.en: one for him and one for her.
chunks.st: the husband, to see if there is any of the wife’s blood on him after intercourse,

chunks.en: The very modest ones get a third one ready,
chunks.st: and one for her, to ascertain after intercourse whether her menstrual flow has begun. And the modest women prepare a third

chunks.en: to get the house ready.
chunks.explain: To check before, so that she can be sure she is tahor.
chunks.st: examination cloth, to examine themselves and prepare the pubic area for intercourse.

summary: If a sign of tumah is found on the checking cloth, this mishnah tells when the husband and wife are tamei and must bring a korban, and when it is only a doubt.

chunks.en: If it was found on his cloth,
chunks.st: If blood was found on his

chunks.en: they are tamei and must bring a korban.
chunks.st: cloth, the woman and her husband are both ritually impure for seven days, in accordance with the halakha of a menstruating woman and of one who engages in intercourse with a menstruating woman, and are each liable to bring a sin offering
chunks.stMore: for unwittingly performing an action punishable with excision from the World-to-Come [karet]. If blood

chunks.en: If it was found on hers right away,
chunks.st: was found on her cloth immediately [otyom]

chunks.en: they are tamei and must bring a korban.
chunks.st: after intercourse, the woman and her husband are likewise ritually impure for seven days and are each liable to bring a sin offering.

chunks.en: If it was found on hers after some time,
chunks.st: If blood was found on her cloth after time

chunks.en: they are tamei because of the doubt, and do not bring a korban.
chunks.st: passed, they are both ritually impure due to uncertainty, as it is possible that the blood appeared only after intercourse, and they are exempt from bringing the sin offering.

summary: This mishnah explains what "after some time" means, and how far back her tumah reaches. Rabbi Akiva and the Sages argue whether her husband also becomes tamei.

chunks.en: What is "after some time"?
chunks.st: What is considered as being: After time passed? It is a period of time equivalent to

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּרֵד מִן הַמִּטָּה וְתָדִיחַ פָּנֶיהָ.
chunks.en: Long enough for her to get down from the bed and wash her face.
chunks.st: the time needed for her to descend from the bed and rinse her face,

chunks.en: And after that,
chunks.st: a euphemism for her pubic area. And afterward, she

chunks.en: she makes things tamei for a full day back, but she does not
chunks.st: retroactively transmits impurity to all ritually pure items with which she came into contact for the preceding twenty-four-hour period, by rabbinic law, but she does not transmit

chunks.en: make her husband tamei.
chunks.st: seven-day impurity to the man with whom she engaged in intercourse.
chunks.stMore: He is impure with this impurity by rabbinic law only until the evening, like one who came in contact with a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says: In the case where blood was found on her cloth after time passed, she even transmits

chunks.en: she even makes her husband tamei.
chunks.st: seven-day impurity by rabbinic law to the man with whom she engaged in intercourse.

chunks.he: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּרוֹאָה כֶתֶם,
chunks.en: And the Sages agree with Rabbi Akiva about a woman who finds a stain,
chunks.st: The mishna concludes: The Rabbis concede to Rabbi Akiva in the case of a woman who sees a blood stain and then engages in intercourse, that she transmits

chunks.en: that she makes her husband tamei.
chunks.st: seven-day impurity to the man with whom she engaged in intercourse, although this impurity also applies by rabbinic law.

summary: A husband may assume his wife is tahor, even when he comes home from a trip. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue how much checking is needed.

chunks.en: All women are assumed to be tahor for their husbands.
chunks.st: All women have the presumptive status of purity for their husbands,
chunks.stMore: and therefore one is not required to ascertain whether his wife is ritually pure before engaging in intercourse with her. Even with regard to husbands

chunks.en: Men who come back from a trip,
chunks.st: returning from a journey,

chunks.en: their wives are assumed to be tahor for them.
chunks.st: if their wives were ritually pure when they left, their wives have the presumptive status of purity for them.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: she needs two checking cloths for
chunks.st: A woman is required to examine herself with two cloths,

chunks.en: each and every time,
chunks.st: once before and once after each and every act of intercourse
chunks.stMore: in which she engages throughout the night, and she must inspect them for blood the following morning,

chunks.en: or she must check by the light of a lamp.
chunks.st: or she must engage in intercourse by the light of a lamp

chunks.en: Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and inspect the cloths before and after each act of intercourse. Beit Hillel say:
chunks.stMore: She is not required to examine herself between each act of intercourse. Rather, it is

chunks.en: two checking cloths are enough for the whole night.
chunks.st: sufficient for her to examine herself with two cloths throughout the night,
chunks.stMore: once before the first act of intercourse and once after the final act of intercourse.

summary: The Sages used a picture of a house with an inner room, a hallway and an upper room, to explain when a sign that is found makes a woman tamei.
stIntro: A woman’s reproductive organs are composed of different parts, and the halakhic status of blood that emerges from one part differs from the halakhic status of blood that emerges from another part.

chunks.en: The Sages gave a comparison about a woman:
chunks.st: The Sages stated a parable with regard to the structure of the sexual organs of a woman, based on the structure of a house: The

chunks.en: the room, the hallway and the upper room.
chunks.st: inner room represents the uterus, and the corridor [perozdor] leading to the inner room represents the vaginal canal, and the upper story

chunks.en: Blood from the room
chunks.st: represents the bladder. Blood from the inner room is ritually impure. Blood

chunks.en: is tamei. If it was found in the hallway,
chunks.st: from the upper story is ritually pure. If blood was found in the corridor,
chunks.stMore: there is uncertainty whether it came from the uterus and is impure, or from the bladder and is pure. Despite

chunks.en: if there is a doubt, it is tamei,
chunks.st: its state of uncertainty, it is deemed definitely impure, due to

chunks.en: because we assume it came from the source.
chunks.st: the fact that its presumptive status is of blood that came from the source, i.e., the uterus, and not from the bladder.

summary: This mishnah lists the five colors that are tamei, and other colors that the Tannaim argue about.

chunks.en: Five kinds of blood are tamei for a woman:
chunks.st: There are five distinct colors of ritually impure blood in a woman:

chunks.en: red, and black,
chunks.st: Red, and black,

chunks.en: and like the bright color of saffron,
chunks.st: and like the bright color of the crocus [karkom]

chunks.en: and like water mixed with earth,
chunks.st: flower, and like water that inundates red earth, and like diluted

chunks.en: and like mixed wine.
chunks.st: wine.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: Even

chunks.he: אַף כְּמֵימֵי תִלְתָּן וּכְמֵימֵי בָשָׂר צָלִי.
chunks.en: also like water of fenugreek, and like the juice of roasted meat.
chunks.st: blood like the water in which a fenugreek plant is soaked, and like the liquid that drips from roast meat,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say these are tahor.
chunks.st: are ritually impure, and Beit Hillel deem blood of those colors ritually pure.

chunks.en: Green: Akavya ben Mahalalel says it is tamei,
chunks.st: With regard to blood that is green, Akavya ben Mahalalel deems

chunks.en: and the Sages say it is tahor.
chunks.st: it impure and the Rabbis deem it pure.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:

chunks.en: even if it does not make tamei as a stain,
chunks.st: Even if the green blood does not transmit impurity due to the halakhot of a blood stain or the blood of a menstruating woman, it is blood in that it renders

chunks.en: it makes tamei as a liquid.
chunks.st: food susceptible to ritual impurity due to its status as one of the seven liquids that render food susceptible to impurity.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yossi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: Neither

chunks.en: not this way and not that way.
chunks.st: in this sense, as the blood of a menstruating woman according to Akavya ben Mahalalel, nor in that
chunks.stMore: sense, as a liquid that renders food susceptible to impurity according to Rabbi Meir, is green blood considered blood.

summary: This mishnah explains each of the five colors that are tamei, comparing each one to something we can see.

chunks.en: What is "red"?
chunks.st: The mishna asks: What is the red

chunks.en: Like the blood of a cut.
chunks.st: color that is impure? It is as red as the blood that flows from a wound.

chunks.en: Black: like ink powder.
chunks.st: What is the black color that is impure? It is blood as black as ḥeret.

words.note: Dark powder used to make ink.

chunks.en: Darker than that
chunks.st: If the black is deeper than that,

chunks.en: is tamei. Lighter than that
chunks.st: the blood is ritually impure; if the black is lighter than that,

chunks.en: is tahor. And like the shine of saffron:
chunks.st: the blood is ritually pure. And what is the color that is like the bright

chunks.en: like its clearest part.
chunks.st: color of the crocus flower that is impure? It is like the brightest part in

chunks.en: And like water mixed with earth:
chunks.st: the flower, which is harvested to produce the orange-colored spice saffron. And what is the color that is like water that inundates red earth

chunks.en: from the valley of Beis Kerem,
chunks.st: that is impure? It is specifically earth from the Beit Kerem Valley and

chunks.en: with water floating over it.
chunks.st: specifically when one inundates

chunks.he: וּכְמָזוּג, שְׁנֵי חֲלָקִים מַיִם וְאֶחָד יַיִן,
chunks.en: And like mixed wine: two parts water and one part wine,
chunks.st: the earth with enough water until it pools on the surface. And what is the color that is like diluted wine that is impure? It is specifically when the dilution consists of two parts water and one part wine,

chunks.en: from the wine of the Sharon.
chunks.st: and specifically when it is from the wine of the Sharon region in Eretz Yisrael.

words.note: A place known for its wine.
